metadata.title: Meta, Amazon: Why this analyst feels 'less confident' in one

content.text:
Amazon (AMZN) and Meta (META) are both set to report quarterly earnings this week.
Wedbush managing director of equity research, Ygal Arounian, shares his expectations for the earnings results.
How about meta? How confident are you, you know, in their role in place in this great AI trade and trend?
So, in general, I'd say we're less confident. Meta has done a phenomenal job of improving their ad products. Uh, there's no question about that and you've seen that in the numbers. Um, and in other areas where, uh, you know, where we like alphabet, right? and on on cloud, uh, custom chips. Meta has been a little bit further behind and now not to say that they can't get this right and and they're not going to build a successful cloud business or a successful chips business and you know, you're starting to see them monetize through uh through subscription tiers on on Instagram and Facebook and uh you know, business AI uh through um, through through WhatsApp. And so some of these things are coming, some of them are a little bit further ahead than others, but it takes a long time to build a successful chip business. It takes a long time to build a successful cloud business. Uh you know, Google keeps talking about how they've been building TPUs for for a decade. They've been doing this business for a decade and they're just starting to make uh external sales to today, right? Uh Amazon's gone through a number of iterations with Tranum before it's become uh what it is today. So, all that takes time. uh building out a cloud business from scratch uh takes a lot of margin. So, you know, we'll see. I think meta has a lot of wood to chop in some of these areas and they're a little bit further behind today.
Amazon, you obviously another company spending very aggressively on AI. What are you expecting from their report? What do you think we see in here?
I I I think we're going to see sort of more of the same. I I I I think there is a real likelihood that CAPEX number, the CAPEX guidance uh gets increased again here. Um, you know, we do think that that uh you'll you'll see good North America retail uh uh numbers. Uh we think that on the margin there's there's room, continued room for improvement driven by advertising and efficiencies that they've laid into the network uh since they've sort of over overbuilt pre-covid and you're seeing those margins come through. I think that that's really important. Um and then the really the big number is going to be AWS acceleration. Uh I would certainly accept expect acceleration there as well. It's just a matter of how much and what that look looks like.
You mentioned North America retail you go. I'm just curious. I mean, oil prices, you know, obviously jumped. What could that mean for for Amazon's transportation costs?
Um, good question. I I I don't have uh a a perfect number for that. it's not built into our numbers. Uh but but they've done enough. Amazon has really done enough uh to to optimize their network uh for for local delivery, fast delivery, um, and we think there's there's plenty of room to offset uh those those oil costs and I think those have also been, you know, they've sort of been in the numbers already since last time we we printed and you maybe even seen some relief there. Uh so not an area that we're overly concerned with.
